sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 1m
facts: Official raster terrain model covers about 99% of England at 1 m resolution
Surface objects are removed to produce a bare-earth DTM
The composite uses the newest best-resolution repeat survey and bilinear interpolation where resampled
The 2022 composite contains surveys from 6 June 2000 to 2 April 2022
sources.limit: Survey age varies spatially; composite metadata alone is not a parcel-specific current-survey guarantee

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 2m
facts: Official terrain model covers about 99% of England at 2 m resolution
Bare-earth surface semantics match the terrain-model role
Repeat-survey selection uses the newest best-resolution source
Metadata indexes identify the survey used at a location
sources.limit: The 2 m layer is only a sensitivity crosscheck and cannot replace the pinned 1 m result

sources.name: LIDAR Composite Digital Terrain Model (DTM) 10m
facts: Official 10 m composite terrain model covers about 99% of England
It is resampled from the 2 m composite using bilinear interpolation
It retains bare-earth terrain semantics
The composite uses survey material from 2000 to 2022
sources.limit: Ten-metre resolution is too coarse for primary sub-metre parcel measurement

sources.name: LIDAR DTM Time Stamped Tiles
facts: Archive contains site-specific surveys at 25 cm, 50 cm, 1 m and 2 m resolutions
GeoTIFF rasters are supplied in 5 km zip files
Heights are in metres relative to Ordnance Datum Newlyn and aligned to the OS Grid
Metadata records survey date, resolution, transformation and geoidal model
sources.limit: Historical tiles cannot be mixed without explicit date, transformation and geoid checks

sources.name: INSPIRE Index Polygons dataset
facts: Dataset contains locations of registered freehold property in England and Wales
Files are separated by local authority
Each polygon has a unique Land Registry INSPIRE ID
Boundary polygons can appear in both neighbouring authority files
sources.limit: The polygon shows indicative extent and position and is not the legal title plan

sources.name: INSPIRE current monthly download
facts: Current package was published 5 July 2026
Files are published on the first Sunday of every month
Downloads are organised by local authority
Use is subject to Open Government Licence conditions
sources.limit: Freshness must be rechecked after the next monthly publication

sources.name: Technical guidance for GML files
facts: Source polygons are captured against British National Grid
Native coordinate reference system is EPSG:27700
Web-map use requires reprojection
British National Grid to WGS84 conversion can shift some features by up to 15 m
sources.limit: Exact containment and raster sampling must remain in native British National Grid

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 documentation
facts: Open height dataset for Great Britain
Product is updated annually in July
Grid uses regular 50 m post spacing
Grid and contour data are supplied in 10 km by 10 km tiles
sources.limit: Landscape-scale product cannot validate a sub-metre parcel height span

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 overview and accuracy
facts: Lower-resolution DTM intended for landscape analysis over large areas
Grid data has regular 50 m post spacing
Grid data was compared with GPS points in sample areas
Published grid accuracy is 4 m RMSE
sources.limit: Four-metre RMSE supports gross-outlier screening only

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 technical specification
facts: Grid and contour forms are created from the same source data
Both forms are supplied as 10 km by 10 km tiles
Grid is available as ASCII and GML 3.2.1
Compressed folders contain data and supporting files
sources.limit: Specification text does not prove the integrity of a particular downloaded archive

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 grid data specification
facts: ASCII tiles contain 200 rows with 200 pixels per row
Each pixel is 50 m by 50 m
Height values are calculated at pixel centres
Heights are supplied to the nearest 0.1 m
sources.limit: Current archive headers and file hashes still require direct byte verification

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 metadata specification
facts: Per-tile XML metadata follows GEMINI conventions
Metadata identifies product and spatial representation
Metadata records the 10 km tile reference
Coordinate-reference context is included
sources.limit: Metadata cannot replace hashes of the outer archive, nested archive and raster files

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 source data
facts: Source terrain is captured as a triangulated irregular network
Grid and contour products are interpolated from the source TIN
Mass points and breaklines retain significant terrain edges
Terrain 50 applies a more generalised representation for small-scale use
sources.limit: Interpolation and generalisation reinforce its coarse crosscheck-only role

sources.name: OS Terrain 50 product supply
facts: Online download is available without registration
ASCII, GML and shapefile full sets are tiled
National data contains 2,858 ten-kilometre tiles
Tiles are arranged in 55 one-hundred-kilometre folders
sources.limit: Supply availability is not evidence that the required TQ archive bytes were retrieved in this runtime

sources.name: Web Coverage Service standard
facts: WCS Core defines mandatory implementation requirements
WCS 2.0.1 is an official core standard
CRS, scaling, range subsetting and interpolation are separate extensions
Coverage access must be assessed against the implemented conformance classes
sources.limit: A standards page does not prove that a specific service response contains correct parcel values

sources.name: WCS 2.0.1 executable compliance test suite
facts: Suite checks GetCapabilities and DescribeCoverage access
GetCoverage KVP behaviour is tested
Mandatory conformance requirements and XML schemas are validated
Core, scaling, interpolation and range-subsetting classes are covered
sources.limit: The generic suite is not evidence that the Environment Agency endpoint was certified by it
